samples.summary: Clear formatting no longer strips `href`, but the HTML-paste ingest path still stores hrefs with no scheme allowlist — unsafe-scheme links now persist in the document with no bulk removal
samples.evidence: Attacker path: a user pastes attacker-authored HTML into a doc. `parseHtmlToBlocks` copies the `<a href>` verbatim into the model with no validation (`packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:610-613`), and `sanitizeInlineStyle` accepts any string href from the internal clipboard payload too (`clipboard.ts:148-149`), so `javascript:`/`data:`/`file:` hrefs are storable and are synced to collaborators via `yorkie-doc-store.ts:139` / `backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:94`. Before this change, `CLEAR_INLINE_STYLE` carried `href: undefined`, so a select-all + Clear formatting scrubbed every pasted link in one action; after the change (`packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:315`, key removed) the only removal command is `removeLink`, which operates on the single link run under the caret (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3719`), i.e. one link at a time. I traced every egress I could find and all of them still gate: ctrl+click and view-only click use `isSafeUrl` (`text-editor.ts:1822`, `2176`), PDF annotations use `isEmittableAnnotationUri` (`pdf-painter.ts:854`), markdown uses `isEmittableUrl` (`serialize/markdown.ts:248`), PPTX export uses `isExportableHref` (`slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:333`), and the popover anchor gates (`docs-link-popover.tsx:217`). So this is defense-in-depth rather than a live XSS: the unsafe value is now durably retained in the model where any future/unaudited consumer of `style.href` becomes the exploit, and the user-facing scrub that used to purge it is gone. Suggested hardening: gate href at ingest (`isSafeUrl` in clipboard.ts, mirroring the PPTX importer's allowlist at `slides/src/import/pptx/text.ts:567`).
searchedFor: grep 'isSafeUrl' repo-wide — checked every call site (text-editor click paths, pdf-painter, markdown, url-detect, docs-link-popover, sheets)
grep 'style.href' across packages/**/src to enumerate every consumer of the stored value
read packages/core/src/url/index.ts for the allowlist implementation
grep for dangerouslySetInnerHTML / innerHTML / '<a href=' in docs, slides, frontend src
grep 'href|hyperlink' in packages/docs/src/export (DOCX emits none; PDF gates)

samples.summary: The new Remove-link button — now the only way to drop a hyperlink on slides/board — calls an optional `removeLink?.()` and is always enabled, so a surface whose editor lacks the method gives silent success on a link the user believes removed
samples.evidence: `removeLink` is declared optional on the shared editor contract (`packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/types.ts:104`) and invoked with optional chaining plus an unconditional `editor.focus()` (`text-format-group.tsx:176`), and the button is deliberately never gated on `getLinkAtCursor()` (comment at lines 168-172). `TextEditSection` hard-codes `showRemoveLink` (`packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.tsx:93`) and is rendered not only by slides but by the board toolbar (`packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-toolbar.tsx:444`) and the mobile Format sheet (`mobile-toolbar.tsx:580`). Since #1051 makes Clear formatting deliberately preserve hyperlinks, this button is the sole removal path on those surfaces; on any surface (present or future) whose editor omits the optional method, the click is a visual no-op and the user is left believing a deceptive/unsafe link was removed when it was not. I confirmed the current slides text-box editor does implement it (`packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:650`), so this is a latent contract weakness rather than a live one — hence low confidence. A required method, or disabling/erroring when absent, would fail loudly instead. (Partly a correctness concern; flagged here because the failure mode is 'user thinks a hostile link is gone'.)
